fields.v: Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen (Liu, He, Li, Du); Pengcheng Laboratory, Shenzhen (Liu, Pan, Xiang, Du); Harbin Institute of Technology, Harbin (Gao), China

Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — benchmark ProjectEval (20 project-level missions, 284 user-interaction-simulation test cases, three input levels) and comparison of 16 LLMs plus OpenHands + GPT-4o under cascade vs direct generation

rev.why: The paper evaluates 16 LLMs, not 15 (8 open-source, 3 code LLMs, 5 closed-source incl. Gemini 2.0-pro; Tables 4, 5, 7 and Appendix B), plus OpenHands + GPT-4o.

fields.v: No SDD approach. Input levels as specification forms: Level 1 NL prompt, Level 2 NL checklist (functions per page), Level 3 code skeleton with docstrings. Generation modes: cascade (agent generates checklist -> skeleton -> code -> parameter values step by step) vs direct (code from the given level). Production agent: OpenHands with GPT-4o (version Not stated); other entries are plain LLMs prompted once

Per mission: Level 1 NL prompt; Level 2 NL checklist (JSON: pages -> functions -> descriptions, LLM-generated and human-reviewed); Level 3 skeleton (canonical code masked); test suite (Selenium or console/file testcodes + parameter descriptions); canonical solution (canonical code + canonical parameter values). Output required as JSON list of files

Cascade mode: NL prompt -> NL checklist -> skeleton -> code -> parameter values (answering the parameter description from own code). Direct mode: given level -> code -> parameter values. Then the evaluator builds the project in a sandbox and runs testcodes with substituted parameter values
None during generation. Human reviewers (third-party company, 8-page guideline) review checklists, canonical code, tests and parameter descriptions during benchmark construction
Specification format only (three input levels: NL prompt, NL checklist, code skeleton) and a staged cascade (checklist -> skeleton -> code), run with LLMs and one agent (OpenHands)
Not classifiable (input formats and a cascade generation mode; authors do not use SDD terms)
New project (whole project generated from scratch from the input)
20 missions (7 from SoftwareDev/ProjectDev, 13 original), 284 test cases (avg 14.2 per mission); canonical answers avg 402.2 LOC and 2,972 tokens
Website projects (mainly Django) and batch/console programs (e.g. Todo app, password generator, Excel-file generation); all canonical code in Python
N/A (no human participants in the evaluation; construction reviewers from a hired third-party company)

Money only for one configuration: the Pass@5 evaluation run with GPT-4o cost USD 28.02 (USD 5.60 per round); no tokens or time per configuration. Benchmark construction costs: GPT-4o USD 2.95, human review USD 420

rev.why: The GPT-4o evaluation cost is a cost of that configuration's run, not only a benchmark cost; the draft said no cost per configuration.

fields.v: Pass@K (K = 1, 5): percentage of the 284 test cases passed (some test cases chained), by user-interaction simulation (Selenium for websites, subprocess for console, file comparison e.g. Openpyxl)
None (maintainability, efficiency and coding practices explicitly not captured)
None

Objective similarity indicators per step: checklist (Sentence Transformer + Jonker-Volgenant), skeleton and code (CodeBLEU + Jonker-Volgenant), parameter values (Levenshtein / string cosine similarity) against canonical artefacts

Automatic: ProjectEval evaluation machine builds the project in a sandbox and runs testcodes; similarity indicators computed automatically. Manual: log examination of failure cases; GPT-4o case study by asking the model for its chain of thought

Criterion: share of test cases passed (no success threshold). Pass@5, all-levels average (cascade L1/L2, direct L1/L2/L3): (a) GPT-4o: 12.49 (best single: direct L1 16.06); Pass@5 run cost USD 28.02 (5.60 per round); (b) Gemini 1.5 pro: 6.65; (c) Gemini 2.0-flash: 4.31; (d) GPT-3.5-turbo: 2.90; (e) Phi-4-14B: 1.13; (f) Gemma-2-9B: 1.06; (g) Mistral-7B-v0.3: 1.00; (h) Gemma-7B: 0.75; (i) Llama-3.1: 0.28; (j) Llama-3.2-3B: 0.10; (k) Llama-2-7B: 0.08; (l) Phi-3-14B: 0.00. Code LLMs, Level 3 direct only: (m) StarCoder-2-7B 0.00; (n) CodeGemma 1.20; (o) CodeLlama 0.77. Pass@1 only: (p) Gemini 2.0-pro: 0.00-7.39 by level; (q) OpenHands + GPT-4o (direct L1): 7.39 (GPT-4o alone 19.72), 8 of 20 tasks not finished (6 AgentStuckInLoopError, 2 not complete); code CodeBLEU 22.96, PV 35.51. All models temperature 0. For every configuration: quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: no criterion stated by the authors for (a) (the only configuration with a cost value); N/A for the others (not measured)

rev.why: Cost was given for GPT-4o (USD 28.02 for the Pass@5 run, p. 6); the draft marked cost N/A for every configuration.

fields.v: Project/tasks: 20 ProjectEval missions. Configurations: 16 LLMs (open-source, closed-source, code LLMs) x input level (L1, L2, L3) x mode (cascade, direct); OpenHands + GPT-4o. Baseline: none (cascade vs direct compared within model). Held constant: missions, prompt template (JSON output), temperature 0, default settings, evaluation machine. Acceptance tests: user-interaction-simulation testcodes validated against the canonical solution (100% pass). Repetitions: Pass@1 and Pass@5 (5 samples); Gemini 2.0-pro and OpenHands Pass@1 only. Human intervention: none (OpenHands runs without user interaction)

rev.why: The paper evaluates 16 LLMs, not 15 (8 open-source, 3 code LLMs, 5 closed-source incl. Gemini 2.0-pro; Tables 4, 5, 7 and Appendix B), plus OpenHands + GPT-4o.

fields.v: GPT-4o best (Pass@5 avg 12.49; only model above 15% at some level); closed-source > open-source; code LLMs near zero; OpenHands + GPT-4o lower than GPT-4o alone (7.39 vs 19.72 Pass@1 direct L1); authors say it beats Gemini 1.5 pro, but on Pass@1 direct L1 both score 7.39 (Table 7), OpenHands is higher only on similarity indicators (Code CodeBLEU 22.96 vs 15.97, PV 35.51 vs 9.99, Table 5). Cascade vs direct: similarity indicators about 2.06% higher for cascade at Level 1, Gemmas, Mistral and Gemini 1.5 pro better with cascade, but GPT-4o better with direct generation on Pass@5; Pass@5 averages: cascade 2.37 vs direct 2.69. Failure causes: invalid JSON output, missing essential files, omitted content. No significance tests

rev.why: 'OpenHands above Gemini 1.5 pro' is not supported by Pass@1: both score 7.39 at direct L1 (Table 7); OpenHands is ahead only on the similarity indicators (Table 5).

fields.v: Distinguished closed vs open-source models; pass rates of most models too low to analyse (authors). Pass@K and CodeBLEU disagree on cascade vs direct, which authors read as execution being more informative than similarity. Repeatability: Pass@5 sampling, no variance or statistics; data, code and evaluation machine released. Limitations stated: Django-centred tasks, Python only, JSON output format may disadvantage some models, canonical parameter values not the only valid answer (Levenshtein penalises valid PV)

Limitations: Django-centred tasks; canonical answers Python only; JSON output format not compatible with all LLMs; canonical parameter values may not be the only answer; running generated code may be harmful; maintainability, efficiency and best practices not captured. Findings: systematic project code generation, overall project understanding and comprehensive analysis are key; formatted output ability matters

Model naming inconsistent: tables say Llama-3.1-7B, Appendix B says Llama3.1-8B; Gemini 2.0 vs Gemini-2.0-pro. Conclusion 'cascade generation is better than direct generation' (p. 8) rests on similarity indicators and conflicts with Pass@5 averages (cascade 2.37 vs direct 2.69, Table 4) and GPT-4o results. Claim that OpenHands + GPT-4o 'still beat the Gemini1.5-pro' (p. 7) not supported by Pass@1: both 7.39 at direct L1 (Table 7); holds only for similarity indicators (Table 5). Benchmark built with GPT-4o, which is also the best model (authors argue Gemini 1.5 pro is close). Difficulty tiers defined but not reported ('no distinction'). Values from Tables 4, 5 and 7. Replication package: https://github.com/RyanLoil/ProjectEval/ (dataset, code, evaluation machine). No pre-registration. Programming language: Python (Django)
